title: Love God, Serve Man -- Ch. 10: Lord, I Am Your Servant
keywords: our hearts are restless until they rest in God
National Union of Students of the Philippines
primary_topics: Chapter 10 of 'Love God, Serve Man' -- the personal 'sharing,' printed here for the first time, in which CJP narrates in candor and vulnerability his own reconversion to the ways of Jesus Christ and how he manifests that new life in his work and leisure.
The Augustinian frame: our hearts are restless until they rest in God, and all of us belong to a ragtag army of walking wounded pretending to be whole while longing for healing, love and peace.

His account of the three false answers he tried to his own restlessness -- academic honors and student leadership, then wealth, then fame -- and how each failed to bring peace, alienating him from his wife and children.

The turning point of 1986, when he was baptized in the Holy Spirit at a Life in the Spirit seminar sponsored by Bukas Loob Sa Diyos, proclaimed Jesus his Lord and Savior, and took up the shepherd's walking stick to bring others to Him.
sub_topics: The opening premise from St. Augustine, and the catalogue of human woundedness -- injured, maimed, insulted, assaulted, afflicted, persecuted, deprived, broken, abandoned and crushed -- that makes everyone a member of an army of walking wounded.
His own strategy of quieting restlessness outside God's way: an angry young man vowing a generous slice of worldly wealth, power and fame to cool his anger and soothe his pains.

The poverty of his childhood: born to poor parents who both died before he could finish schooling, sleeping on cold sidewalks, selling newspapers, shining shoes and peddling textbooks to classmates to be able to own one himself, educated in public schools and a non-sectarian university, and though baptized a Catholic having no idea of the Christian faith.

The rewards of voracious study: Latin honors, acclaim as 'Most Outstanding Student,' bar topnotcher, president of the University Central Student Council, co-founder and head of the National Union of Students of the Philippines, and a student-hero on campus.

The discovery after graduation that academic honors and student leadership did not satisfy his thirst for life, love, gratification and happiness -- and the embittered vow, after an episode of want, that travel would never again hinder his ambitions and that one day he would be super rich and control other people's lives.

The search in earthly treasures: witnessing the ultra-rapid amassing of wealth in Hong Kong in the early '80s, serving as counsel in transactions involving billions of Hong Kong dollars, enjoying first class travel, private jets and yachts, Rolls-Royce limousines, Piaget and Patek Philippe watches and the mansions of the rich and famous -- and seeing that wealth vanish in the 1982 Hong Kong stock market crash.

The search in fame: becoming a fixture in high-society gossip and society columns, which brought no peace, no fulfillment and no sense of purpose, and alienated him from his wife and children while the questions persisted -- who am I, why was I born, where am I headed for?

The turning point of 1986: finding Jesus Christ, baptism in the Holy Spirit at a BLD Life in the Spirit seminar, proclaiming Jesus Lord, Savior, Healer and Friend, learning that his purpose is to obey and glorify Him, and becoming in St. Paul's words 'a new creation.'

Life in imitation of Christ as a recurring cycle of passion, death and resurrection -- his passion in the long search for meaning, and his need to die to pride, private ambitions and human aspirations in order to rise.

The quoted portion of his earlier sharing: having met both the high and the lowly, the powerful and the weak, the 'glitterati' and the downtrodden, he knows their emptiness and loneliness, sees them as lost sheep without the Good Shepherd, and has imposed on himself the duty of taking up the shepherd's walking stick despite feeling inadequate and unworthy, since it is by faith and not by sight that he found the Lord.

The consequent discipline of Scripture: reading the Bible cover to cover many times and volumes of commentaries, researching the Holy Father's teaching and encyclicals, making the Scriptures his guide in law practice, business, home, leisure and lifestyle, and developing with BLD the gifts of discernment, sharing, reflection, prayer and healing.

The fruits he ascribes to surrender since 1986: a happy home, advancement in his profession, and 'evangelical prosperity' providing his family's needs and his children's education in the best Philippine schools and graduate degrees abroad.

The closing confession of unworthiness: still a sinner thoroughly unworthy of God's blessings, seeing only the compassionate and merciful eyes of Jesus, abandoning all he is and has before Him, and taking refuge in St. Paul's First Letter to Timothy, quoted in full, where the former blasphemer and persecutor is made a servant and judged faithful.

one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 10 of 'Love God, Serve Man' prints for the first time the personal 'sharing' in which Atty. Artemio V. Panganiban narrates his own reconversion to the ways of Jesus Christ. He begins with St. Augustine's line that our hearts are restless until they rest in God, and argues that all of us, having been injured, insulted, afflicted, broken or crushed, belong to a ragtag army of walking wounded pretending to be whole and healthy. In his own case, he says, he tried to quiet that restlessness outside God's way: an angry young man, he vowed a generous slice of worldly wealth, power and fame. He recounts a childhood of poverty -- parents who both died before he finished schooling, sleeping on cold sidewalks, selling newspapers, shining shoes, peddling textbooks to classmates so he could own one, educated in public schools and a non-sectarian university and, though baptized a Catholic, with no idea of the Christian faith. Voracious study brought Latin honors, acclaim as Most Outstanding Student, a place at the top of the bar, the presidency of the University Central Student Council and the leadership of the National Union of Students of the Philippines; but he learned right after graduation that honors and student leadership did not satisfy his thirst for life and love, and he vowed instead to become super rich. In Hong Kong in the early '80s he was counsel in transactions involving billions of Hong Kong dollars and enjoyed private jets, yachts, Rolls-Royce limousines and Patek Philippe watches, only to watch such wealth vanish in the 1982 crash and to find that the lavish life-style merely increased his appetite for more; fame in the society columns likewise brought no peace and alienated him from his wife and children. The turning point came in 1986, when he was baptized in the Holy Spirit at a Life in the Spirit seminar sponsored by Bukas Loob Sa Diyos, proclaimed Jesus his Lord and Savior, and became 'a new creation.' Understanding life in Christ as a recurring cycle of passion, death and resurrection, he had to die to his pride and ambitions; and because his resurrection would be incomplete if he alone found God, he took up the shepherd's walking stick, read the Bible cover to cover and made Scripture his guide in law, business, home and leisure. He closes by ascribing his happy home, professional advancement and 'evangelical prosperity' to surrender, confessing himself still a sinner thoroughly unworthy of God's blessings, and quoting St. Paul's First Letter to Timothy, where the former blasphemer and persecutor is made a servant and judged faithful.
